findings.reason: Fresh-context review reproduced that a parseable run.started line is visible before fsync completes and before Session.run enters its KeyboardInterrupt handler. The test now waits for an explicit ready marker written at the start of the stubbed turn, which proves the intended interrupt point was reached.

reviewed_evidence: C: exact main 4019525 run 43038668272 failed Ubuntu Python 3.13 in tests/test_skeleton.py:154 after observing the trace path but before run.started was durably appended; the trace ended at run.started or had no terminal event.

V: local high-frequency reproduction on macOS CPython 3.13.9 sent SIGINT as soon as the trace path appeared and reproduced the same run.started-only/KeyboardInterrupt-during-append failure within 5-10 iterations.

R: fresh-context review found that waiting only for a parseable run.started event is still insufficient because TraceRecorder flushes before fsync and Session.run enters its handler only after append returns; an in-memory delayed-fsync probe reproduced the remaining failure.
C: the stubbed turn now writes an explicit readiness marker as its first action; the test delivers SIGINT only after that marker exists, so it interrupts the in-flight turn rather than trace startup.
V: the corrected focused test passed 100/100 consecutive local repetitions; the complete tests.test_skeleton module passed 16/16; Ruff E9/F, compileall and git diff --check passed.
U: exact-head CI for this test-only repair and merged-main readback remain pending.

R: final fresh-context review of commit 7f26f69 found no actionable regressions; it confirmed the readiness marker is created inside the stubbed turn after Session.run enters its interrupt-handling block and the cancellation assertions remain unchanged.
unverified_scope: This test-only change does not alter runtime behavior, provider calls, packaging, release artifacts, tags, Releases or uploads. It removes the observed test race but does not claim that arbitrary SIGINT timing during trace I/O is a supported product behavior.
